

| Step | Instruction | Interaction | Hint text |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 6-8-6-1-1 | Sort each of these values into the correct bucket. | Numbers on tiles that can be dragged into a bucket: 3, 5, 1, 8, 1, 4, 7\. Two buckets labeled 1-5, 6-10. Tiles stack on top of each other (so the end result look like a histogram). |  |
| 6-8-6-1-2 | This is called a *histogram* (HIST-o-gram). Tap the bucket with the most values in it? | Same histogram. Buckets are selectable. Target 1-5. |  |
| 6-8-6-1-3 | Real histograms don’t show buckets. But they still call the range of values for each bar a bucket. Which bucket here has the *least* values in it? | Histogram of 1-3, 4-6, 7-9, 10-12 with heights 2, 6, 4, 1\. Bars are selectable. Target 10-12. | The bucket with the least values in it is the shortest. |
| 6-8-6-1-4 | Dot plots are great if you have 12 or 20 dots, but not if you have 100 or 1,000. Which of these data sets will be very large? | Multiple choice: Class votes for favorite band; The weight of every dog in Chicago. Target: the weight of every dog in Chicago. |  |
| 6-8-6-1-5 | For large data sets, histograms are better. This bar shows the number of US states with a population between 0 and 5 million. How many are there? | This histogram with only the left-most bar showing. Add an arrow pointing to the top of the first bar. Multiple choice: 5, 29, 50\. Target: 29\.![][image1] | The height of the bar tells you how many states. |
| 6-8-6-1-6 | Think of a bar as being like a stack of dots. How many states have populations between 5 and 10 million? | Same histogram, now revealing the second bar. Put 15 dots inside the second bar. Multiple choice: 5, 10, 15\. Target: 15\. | You can count the dots but it’s quicker to read off the total. |
| 6-8-6-1-7 | Agree or disagree: the largest state has more than 40 million people? | Whole histogram. No dots. Multiple choice: Agree, Disagree. Target, Disagree | The short bar on the right has between 35 and 40 million people. |
| 6-8-6-1-8 | This histogram shows the number of pages Mia read on 30 nights. Tap the bar containing the most pages she read in one night? | Make a histogram 0-5 (4), 6-10 (9), 11-15 (11), 16-20 (6). Text box. Bars are selectable. Target 16-20. | Think about it: is the most she read the tallest bar or the bar farthest right? |
| 6-8-6-1-9 | Look at the bar in the 0-5 bucket. Agree or disagree: Mia could have read 0 pages one night? | Same histogram. Agree and Disagree buttons. Target: Agree. | 0-5 means values in that bar could be anything from 0 to 5\. |
| 6-8-6-1-10 | Agree or disagree: Mia read between 0 and 5 pages on the same number of nights as she read between 10 and 15 pages. | Same histogram. Agree and Disagree buttons. Target: Disagree. |  |
